**Assumptions practitioners hold, and their negations**

1. More 3x3 convolutions are always better. If false, a conv edit hurts or saturates when conv capacity already exists on a parallel path.
2. Effects of edits are additive. If false, the same edit gains or loses depending on neighbouring edges, e.g. a conv after a pool differs from a conv after a conv.
3. More input-to-output paths always help. If false, duplicate paths of the same type add redundancy or optimization noise.
4. Skip connections are always good. If false, a skip duplicates an existing identity route or merges raw features into a node that wanted processed ones.
5. Pooling is a weak, harmful op. If false, pooling acts as a useful smoother or regularizer when it sits next to convs.
6. A larger kernel is better than a smaller one. If false, 1x1 is better or equal when a 3x3 already supplies spatial context.
7. Deeper chains are better. If false, depth through edges 0, 2 and 5 hurts unless a shortcut exists.
8. Removing an edge always hurts. If false, removal is harmless or helpful when an equivalent route exists.

I have not checked these hypotheses against benchmark data.
